newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares close lower in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares close lower in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower in thin trading for the third consecutive day on Wednesday, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.89 percent, or 2.23 points, to 249.47 on low all-share turnover of 97 million shekels against 99 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.88 percent lower at 255.92.

"The market continues to show weakness and volume is low," said Michael Politzer at the Central Securities Corp. "The market rose sharply at the beginning of the year and it reached a point where it couldn't rise any further. On the other hand there is also no reason for a dramatic decline."
"The market is sleepy. Foreign investors have reduced their activity and everybody is waiting for further political developments," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.

"Investors are also waiting for the CPI release and it seems now that the Bank of Israel will leave its key lending rate unchanged in the coming months. I believe that the Maof will remain between 250 and 260 for the next few days," Politzer added.
Analysts predict the February consumer price index, to be released on Friday, will show a 1.2 percent rise over January.

Supersol plunged 4.5 percent to 966 agorot. The company said on Wednesday that 1996 net profit rose to 102.7 million shekels from 92.7 million in 1995, but traders said Supersol is expected to suffer an earnings decline as the economy slows.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 1.25 percent to 30,808 agorot on volume of 7.2 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which lost 1.25 percent to 628 agorot on turnover of 3.5 million shekels; and IDB Holdings, which fell 1.25 percent to 6,473 agorot on volume of 3.4 million shekels.
